    38	# Commission Calculator Constitution
    39	
    40	## Core Principles
    41	
    42	### I. Payout Ambiguity Is the Maintainer's Decision (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
    43	
    44	Any ambiguity whose resolution changes what any rep is paid — by any amount, in any scenario — is
    45	decided by the maintainer, in writing, and never by an assumption, a default, an "industry
    46	standard" or an informed guess. This overrides two SpecKit defaults for such ambiguities: the
    47	specify step's instruction to make informed guesses, and its cap of three
    48	`[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers. Every payout-affecting ambiguity gets a marker, however many there
    49	are, and clarify is re-run past its per-session question cap until a run finds none left.
    50	
    51	Each question put to the maintainer shows a worked scenario in which the readings produce
    52	different dollar amounts, the options, and a recommendation. The maintainer's answer is recorded in
    53	`spec.md` verbatim. An ambiguity discovered later — in planning, in implementation, or by a test —
    54	stops the work and goes back to the maintainer; it is never resolved in code.
    55	
    56	Ambiguities that cannot change a payout (layout, wording, which scenario is selected by default)
    57	follow SpecKit's normal defaults.
    58	
    59	*Rationale:* a commission rule written in prose has several defensible readings, and each reading
    60	is a different paycheck. An agent's "reasonable" choice is still a compensation-policy decision
    61	made by someone with no authority to make it.
    62	
    63	### II. Test-First, Exact to the Cent (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
    64	
    65	- Red-green-refactor without exception: a test is written and watched failing before the code that
    66	  makes it pass. No implementation code is written before `/speckit-implement`.
    67	- Every concrete example in an acceptance scenario has a test that exercises that exact example —
    68	  the same inputs, and the expected amount asserted to the cent. A representative or "equivalent"
    69	  substitute does not satisfy this. If an example turns out to be unachievable as written, that is a
    70	  spec defect and goes back to the maintainer (Principle I).
    71	- Unit tests use the test framework's own idiom. Integration tests are Gherkin feature files whose
    72	  scenarios mirror `spec.md`'s acceptance scenarios; the BDD tool is confirmed to be currently
    73	  maintained, with the date and source recorded, before it is adopted.
    74	- A test guarding a failure path (rejected input, refund clawback, draw recovery) is watched failing
    75	  with the guarded behaviour removed, and the observed result is recorded.
    76	- A test is never changed to make it pass. A test that looks wrong means the spec is wrong: stop and
    77	  raise it with the maintainer.
    78	- No false greens: no silent or conditional skips; the suite reports every test it did not run, by
    79	  name and reason, and CI fails on any skip. Every test passes run alone and in any order, against
    80	  no mutable shared state it did not create; reading files committed to the repository (seed
    81	  data, the spec) is allowed.
    82	- Coverage is reported on every CI run. 100% is the aim; below 80% line coverage of the engine is
    83	  a defect. Coverage is a by-product: a test that asserts nothing is forbidden.
    84	
    85	*Rationale:* a payout that is off by a cent in one tier boundary is invisible in a happy-path test
    86	and obvious in an exact one. The examples in the spec are the maintainer's own statement of what
    87	correct means; testing an easier substitute quietly narrows it.
    88	
    89	### III. Spec Fidelity and Traceability
    90	
    91	- Every change that alters calculated payouts, what a test proves, or the application's behaviour
    92	  goes through the SpecKit pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → tasks → analyze → implement).
    93	  Scope is decided by stakes, not by calling something a fix; an exemption granted once is not a
    94	  precedent.
    95	- Clarify and analyze are mandatory for every feature. Analyze runs until a pass is clean or the
    96	  remediate loop reaches a stop condition.
    97	- Every number in a spec is tagged as a requirement or a placeholder to be measured.
    98	- Every functional requirement (FR) and success criterion (SC) traces to the member that implements
    99	  it and to the tests that verify it. Every test of product behaviour names the FR/SC it verifies;
   100	  a test of project tooling (CI gates, generators) names the constitution principle it enforces
   101	  instead, and the traceability report lists such tests in their own section. Every line of a
   102	  payout breakdown shown to a user cites the FR that produced it. The trace is generated from test
   103	  metadata by a script, never maintained by hand, and any FR/SC with no test or no implementation is
   104	  listed as a gap.
   105	
   106	*Rationale:* a payout the user cannot trace to a rule cannot be checked, and a trace kept by hand
   107	drifts from the code the first time nobody updates it.
   108	
   109	### IV. Evidence Before Assertion
   110	
   111	- Every load-bearing claim in `research.md`, and every fact in this constitution about the world
   112	  outside the repository, records how it was established — measured, spiked, decompiled, read from
   113	  the vendor's current documentation (with the date consulted), assumed, or copied from a named
   114	  source and not independently verified — and when. A claim does not gain authority by being moved
   115	  into a more trusted document; a hedge stays a hedge unless new evidence is recorded with it.
   116	- Perishable claims carry a revisit trigger.
   117	- A claim that something is absent, impossible, or untestable meets the same bar as a claim that it
   118	  is present, and needs a positive control.
   119	- This applies in conversation as well as in documents: a statement about what a library does, or
   120	  what a change would touch, is checked in the same turn or stated with its uncertainty.
   121	
   122	*Rationale:* the fidelity gates check that artifacts agree with each other, not that they are true.
   123	Evidence is the only check on truth, and it has to be visible on the page to the next reader.
   124	
   125	### V. Clean Architecture and Warnings-as-Errors
   126	
   127	- The commission engine is a plain library with no dependency on the web framework, UI, file system
   128	  or clock. The dependency rule points inward: the web app depends on the engine, never the
   129	  reverse. The UI renders the engine's breakdown and never recomputes or adjusts an amount.
   130	- Money is represented exactly (no binary floating point anywhere a monetary amount is held or
   131	  computed). Where rounding happens and to what precision is a spec decision under Principle I.
   132	- Warnings are build errors, identically locally and in CI, from the first commit.
   133	- SOLID and DRY apply; a trade-off against a SOLID principle is flagged, not silently resolved.
   134	  No speculative abstractions, configuration or error handling for cases the spec does not require.
   135	  Input is validated at the boundary (seeded scenario data); internal code trusts its callers.
   136	
   137	*Rationale:* the engine is the thing whose correctness matters; keeping it free of framework
   138	concerns is what makes it exhaustively unit-testable and lets the UI be a thin, honest view of it.
   139	
   140	### VI. Accessible by Default
   141	
   142	The UI meets WCAG 2.2 AA as a baseline: semantic HTML, a label for every control, full keyboard
   143	operation with visible focus, sufficient colour contrast, data tables with header cells, and no
   144	information conveyed by colour alone. An accessibility gap in UI being touched is a defect.
   145	
   146	*Rationale:* the breakdown is the product; a breakdown a screen-reader user cannot navigate is a
   147	breakdown that does not exist for them.

   150	
   151	The application's runtime environment is a developer machine running `dotnet run`. Any change that
   152	makes startup or a request path depend on something new — an environment variable, a file, a
   153	service, a port — is an explicit task that wires it into every place the app is run (the run
   154	instructions and CI), or the task list states in one line that the feature adds none. No degraded
   155	window (cold start, pause, reclaimed instance) is accepted, because nothing is deployed; a feature
   156	that introduces one must map it to an FR or SC.
   157	
   158	*Rationale:* "works on the machine that wrote it" is not the same as "runs with `dotnet run` from a

   222	## Development Workflow & Quality Gates
   223	
   224	- **Approval per action.** Commit only when the maintainer asks. Push, and merge a PR, only with
   225	  explicit approval for that specific action; an earlier approval does not carry forward.
   226	- **Main is reached only through a pull request** after the initial ratification push. Every
   227	  tasks.md phase is its own branch and PR; no PR spans two phases, and no phase starts before the
   228	  previous one is merged. Merges are squash-merges, deleting the branch.

   231	  a change that "cannot" have broken anything is investigated as a finding, not retried as flake.

   406	### Edge Cases
   407	
   408	- A deal amount, quota or refund of zero or less; any monetary input (deal amount, quota, refund,
   409	  opening recoverable balance) that is not a whole number of cents; a negative opening recoverable
   410	  balance; or a split percentage that is not greater than 0% and at most 100% (requirement): the
   411	  scenario is rejected with a message; no payouts are shown for it (FR-004).
   412	- A deal in the scenario's own deal list (counted or not) credited to a rep who is not on the
   413	  roster: rejected (FR-004). Booking-
   414	  quarter data supplied for clawbacks may name reps not on the roster (with their start dates);
   415	  they get no statement (FR-016).
   416	- A scenario quarter that is not exactly three (requirement) whole calendar months starting on the
   417	  first day of a month: rejected (FR-014 counts draws per calendar month).
   418	- A refund dated before the deal's booking date: rejected.
   419	- A rep whose start date is after the quarter's last day: the scenario is rejected, naming the rep
   420	  (FR-011).
   421	- A deal booked before the start date of a rep credited on it, whether or not the deal counts this
   422	  quarter: the scenario is rejected, naming the deal and the rep (FR-011).
   423	- Amounts that do not divide to whole cents (e.g. 5% of $10.10 (requirement) is $0.505
   424	  (requirement)): rounded per FR-018 to $0.51 (US1 AS4).
   425	- A partial refund: clawed back per FR-017. A refund of zero or less, or refunds on one deal
   426	  totalling more than the deal amount, are rejected.
   427	- A clawback larger than the commission earned in the quarter: earned commission goes negative
   428	  and the magnitude is added to the closing recoverable balance (FR-015, FR-016).

   430	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
   431	
   432	### Functional Requirements
   433	
   434	**Scenarios and display**
   435	
   436	- **FR-001**: The system MUST offer a list of seeded scenarios and let the user select one.
   437	- **FR-002**: For the selected scenario, the system MUST show every rep in it with their quota,
   438	  credited bookings, attainment, earned commission, draws paid, recovery, clawbacks, commission
   439	  payable and closing recoverable balance. Attainment is shown as a percentage to two decimal
   440	  places (requirement), rounded half away from zero; it is display only and never used to compute
   441	  an amount.
   442	- **FR-003**: Each rep's result MUST include a line-by-line breakdown in which every amount is on
   443	  its own line and each line cites the FR ID of the rule that produced it — including the subtotals
   444	  "Credited bookings" (FR-008) and "Draws paid" (FR-014) and, after each refund on a split deal, the
   445	  rep's re-split share (FR-017), as Appendix A shows.
   446	- **FR-004**: A scenario that violates a validation rule (FR-011, FR-013, Edge Cases) MUST be shown
   447	  as rejected with the reasons, and MUST NOT show any payout. Every monetary input MUST be a whole
   448	  number of cents; deal amounts, quotas and refunds MUST be greater than zero; an opening
   449	  recoverable balance MUST be zero or more; every split percentage MUST be greater than 0%
   450	  (requirement) and at most 100% (requirement). A scenario MUST also be rejected, naming the rep,
   451	  deal or quarter involved, when: its roster is empty; two roster reps share a repId; two deals in
   452	  one quarter's deal list share a dealId; a rep appears more than once on one deal; a prorated quota rounds to $0.00 (requirement); any deal in the
   453	  scenario's own deal list (counted or not) is credited to a rep not on the roster; a deal
   454	  refunded in the quarter was booked in an earlier quarter whose data is missing or incomplete
   455	  (complete means: for each roster rep credited on the deal, that quarter's dates, their quota,
   456	  start date, all their deals booked in it, and every refund on those deals dated before the
   457	  refund being sized, whatever quarter that earlier refund falls in; for a split partner not on the
   458	  roster, their start date), is not three whole calendar months, overlaps the scenario's quarter, or
   459	  contains a deal booked outside its own dates; or a rep's start date in booking-quarter data
   460	  differs from the roster's; or an earlier-quarter deal listed both in the scenario's own deal
   461	  list and in booking-quarter data differs between the two.
   462	
   463	**Quota and rates**
   464	
   465	- **FR-005**: Each rep MUST have a quarterly quota in USD, greater than zero.
   466	- **FR-006**: Commission MUST be tiered on quota attainment at 5% (requirement) up to 100%
   467	  (requirement) of quota, 8% (requirement) from 100% to 150% (requirement), and 12%
   468	  (requirement) above 150%, applied marginally: each slice of credited bookings earns its own
   469	  band's rate, and each band with a non-zero slice is its own breakdown line.
   470	- **FR-007**: Band edges are at exactly 100% (requirement) and 150% (requirement) of quota: the 5%
   471	  band covers credited bookings up to and including 100% of quota, the 8% band the part above 100%
   472	  up to and including 150%, and the 12% band the part above 150% (rates and edges as tagged in
   473	  FR-006). (Under marginal tiers the edge assignment cannot
   474	  change an amount; it fixes which line a slice appears on.)
   475	- **FR-008**: A deal MUST count toward the quarter in which its booking date falls (first and last
   476	  day inclusive); its close date does not affect crediting and is shown for information only.
   477	  Deals booked outside the quarter are excluded and listed with the reason.
   478	- **FR-009**: Attainment MUST be the rep's credited bookings divided by the rep's (prorated, where
   479	  FR-010 applies) quota.
   480	
   481	**Proration**
   482	
   483	- **FR-010**: A rep whose start date is after the first day of the quarter MUST have their quota
   484	  prorated by calendar days: full quota × (days from the start date to the quarter's last day,
   485	  both inclusive) ÷ (days in the quarter, both ends inclusive).
   486	- **FR-011**: A scenario in which any deal — counted this quarter or not, including booking-quarter
   487	  data supplied for clawbacks — is credited to a rep whose start date is after that deal's booking
   488	  date MUST be rejected, naming the deal and the rep. A scenario listing a rep whose
   489	  start date is after the quarter's last day MUST be rejected, naming the rep.
   490	
   491	**Splits**
   492	
   493	- **FR-012**: A deal MAY be split between reps; each rep's credited share is the deal amount times
   494	  their split percentage. The share, and only the share, counts toward that rep's credited
   495	  bookings — both for attainment and for commission — so credit across all reps sums to the deal
   496	  amount. Shares are allocated to the cent by largest remainder: each share is first rounded down
   497	  to the cent, then the leftover cents are given one at a time to the shares with the largest
   498	  fractional remainders, ties going to the rep listed first on the deal. After a refund, the
   499	  same allocation re-splits the reduced deal amount across the deal's reps (FR-017). This is the one exception to
   500	  FR-018's half-away-from-zero rounding.
   501	- **FR-013**: A deal's split percentages MUST sum to exactly 100% (requirement); otherwise the
   502	  scenario is rejected.
   503	
   504	**Draw**
   505	
   506	- **FR-014**: Each rep MUST receive a draw of $4,000.00 (requirement) for each calendar month of
   507	  the quarter in which they are employed. In the month containing a mid-quarter start date the
   508	  draw is $4,000.00 (requirement) × (days from the start date to that month's last day, both inclusive) ÷ (days
   509	  in that month); months before the start month carry no draw. Each month's draw is its own
   510	  breakdown line.
   511	- **FR-015**: Each rep has an opening recoverable balance (default $0.00, requirement) of draw not yet
   512	  recovered from earlier quarters. The recoverable total is that balance plus the draws paid this
   513	  quarter. Earned commission is commission before refunds minus clawbacks, and may be negative.
   514	  When earned commission is zero or more, the amount recovered is the lesser of earned commission
   515	  and the recoverable total, commission payable is earned commission minus the amount recovered,
   516	  and the closing recoverable balance is the recoverable total minus the amount recovered. When
   517	  earned commission is negative, the amount recovered and commission payable are $0.00 and the
   518	  closing recoverable balance is the recoverable total plus the negative amount's magnitude.
   519	  Commission payable is never negative. Each of these is its own breakdown line.
   520	
   521	**Refunds**
   522	
   523	- **FR-016**: When a deal is refunded, the commission on that deal MUST be clawed back, one line
   524	  per refund, in the statement of the quarter containing the refund date, and sized per FR-017.
   525	  A scenario includes, for any deal refunded in its quarter but booked in an earlier one, that
   526	  booking quarter's data for the affected reps (quarter dates, quota, start date, deals, and every
   527	  earlier refund on those deals, whatever quarter it is dated in). That data may name split partners who are not on this quarter's roster; they
   528	  are listed with their start dates and receive no statement. A refund dated after the scenario's quarter ends has no effect on that
   529	  quarter's statement.
   530	- **FR-017**: A deal MAY have several refunds, each partial or full, as long as they total no
   531	  more than the deal amount. For each rep, all refunds on deals booked in the same quarter are
   532	  applied in refund-date order across deals; refunds on the same date are ordered by their deal's
   533	  position in that quarter's deal list, then by their position within the deal. (The order can
   534	  move an amount between two clawback lines but never changes their total.) Each refund's clawback is
   535	  that booking quarter's commission computed with every earlier refund applied, minus the same
   536	  quarter computed with this refund also applied; a refunded amount no longer counts toward
   537	  attainment. On a split deal, after each refund the reduced deal amount (the deal amount minus
   538	  all refunds applied so far) is re-split across its reps by FR-012's largest-remainder
   539	  allocation, and each rep's clawback is computed from their re-split credit. A full refund is the
   540	  case where the refunds total the deal amount. A clawback is exactly the recomputed difference
   541	  and may be negative, when a re-split raises a rep's credit.
   542	
   543	**Money**
   544	
   545	- **FR-018**: Every computed monetary amount — prorated quota, the 150% (requirement) band edge,
   546	  prorated draw, each tier line, clawback, recovery — MUST be rounded to the cent when it is
   547	  produced, half away from zero, and later steps MUST use the rounded value. Every total MUST
   548	  equal the sum of the lines shown. Split shares are the exception and follow FR-012.
   549	- **FR-019**: All amounts MUST be in USD. Tax, currency conversion and multi-year contract handling
   550	  are out of scope.
   551	
   552	**Application**
   553	
   554	- **FR-020**: The application MUST run locally from a single command, with no external services,
   555	  no authentication, and no database beyond in-memory data or a local file.
   556	- **FR-021**: The interface MUST be operable by keyboard alone and by screen reader, with the
   557	  breakdown presented as a table with header cells.
   558	
   559	### Key Entities
   560	
   561	- **Scenario**: a named, seeded quarter (a first and last date), its roster of reps, its deals,
   562	  and any booking-quarter data needed to size clawbacks for refunds dated in the quarter.
   563	- **Rep**: name, quarterly quota (USD), start date, and opening recoverable draw balance (USD,
   564	  default $0.00; FR-015).
   565	- **Deal**: identifier, amount (USD), close date, booking date, one or more split credits (rep and
   566	  percentage, in listed order), and zero or more refunds (amount and date).
   567	- **Commission result**: per rep — prorated quota, credited bookings, attainment, and the ordered
   568	  breakdown lines, each with amount, description and the citing FR ID.

   584	  a pointing device (requirement).

   588	- Each scenario states its own quarter as a first and last date, so no fiscal calendar is assumed.

   591	- Scenarios are read-only seeded data; editing or creating scenarios is out of scope.
   592	- Only the rules in the brief apply: no accelerators, caps, SPIFs, or rep terminations mid-quarter.

    15	FR citations (web-host tests are Gherkin too, in the Specs project). CI (GitHub Actions) is the
    16	review gate. Evidence for each choice is in
    17	[research.md](research.md).

   447	- Phases run strictly in order 1 → 9; each starts only after the previous phase's PR is merged
   448	  (standing rule 4). Stories are sequential for one reviewer even where independent.
   449	- Within a phase: test tasks first (seen failing), then implementation; `[P]` test tasks can be
   450	  written together.
   451	- US1 (MVP) delivers the page and tier lines with FR citations, verified against test-created
   452	  scenario folders; the shipped app shows "No scenarios are installed" until Phase 9.
   453	- US2–US6 each add their rules. Polish writes the full-statement check (SC-001) first, sees it fail,
   454	  then adds the eleven seed files it checks (T060, T060a) — so seed contents are test-driven.

1	# Research: Quarterly Sales Commission Calculator
     2

    23	  reader out of the box, needs no JavaScript and makes every scenario a linkable URL.

    25	  template's static assets are local under `wwwroot/lib` (no CDN). The `lang` attribute on the
    26	  rendered `<html>` was read by a test (AngleSharp) through `WebApplicationFactory`.
    27	- **Alternatives**: Blazor Server (needs a live SignalR circuit and JavaScript for a static
    28	  read-only view — no benefit); minimal API + static HTML (would need client script to render).

    31	
    32	- **Decision**: xUnit v3 `xunit.v3` 4.0.1 on **Microsoft.Testing.Platform (MTP)**, opted in via
    33	  `global.json` `"test": { "runner": "Microsoft.Testing.Platform" }`. No `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`,

    37	  is no longer supported by Microsoft.Testing.Platform on .NET 10 SDK and later"; with the
    38	  `global.json` opt-in the same project runs.

    40	  memory of the usual template; that combination does not run. Kept visible because the difference
    41	  in method is the lesson (Principle IV).

    47	  2026-09-21 — NuGet: `Reqnroll`/`Reqnroll.xUnit.v3` 3.3.4 published 2026-03-23; GitHub
    48	  `reqnroll/Reqnroll`: not archived, last push 2026-08-26, most recent commit 2026-08-26 ("added

    56	- **Revisit when**: a Reqnroll release declares support for a newer xUnit major, or xUnit v3's

    58	
    59	## R5. No silent skips
    60	
    61	- **Decision**: every CI test run passes `--fail-skips on`.
    62	- **Established**: spiked. Without it, a test marked `Skip` produced "Test run summary: Passed!"

    89

    91	  `coverage-gate` and `list-tests`, unit-tested by `tests/CommissionCalculator.Tools.Tests`. `trace`

    99	  stands; it is no longer relied on.
   100

   102

   105	- **Established**: registry 2026-09-21; spiked — a test fetched `/` and asserted `lang="en"`.
   106	
   107	## R10. Exact money arithmetic
   108	
   109	- **Decision**: all money is `decimal`; rounding is
   110	  `Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)` (FR-018); whole-cent validation is
   111	  `decimal.Round(x, 2) == x`; percentages are `decimal`.
   112	- **Established**: spiked — `Math.Round(0.505m, 2, AwayFromZero)` = 0.51 and of −0.505m = −0.51;
   113	  `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<decimal>("10.005")` = 10.005 exactly (scale 3), so a sub-cent input
   114	  is detectable after deserialization (FR-004).

   116	## R11. Dates
   117	
   118	- **Decision**: `DateOnly`; inclusive day counts as `end.DayNumber − start.DayNumber + 1`.
   119	- **Established**: spiked — 2026-05-16..2026-06-30 = 46 (spec US3 AS3).

   122	
   123	- **Finding**: spiked — with a solution file at the repository root, `dotnet run` there fails:
   124	  "Couldn't find a project to run … or pass the path to the project using --project."
   125	- **Decision**: the web project is the only runnable project; run it with
   126	  `dotnet run --project src/CommissionCalculator.Web` from the root, or plain `dotnet run` from
   127	  `src/CommissionCalculator.Web`. Both are documented in the README; CI exercises the first (the
   128	  smoke step starts the app with `--project` and requests `/`). Putting the web `.csproj` at the root was rejected: its
   129	  default file globs would compile the engine, tests and tools into the web assembly.

   131	  2026-09-21 ("2: yes", plan.md decision 2).

   134	
   135	- **Decision**: one JSON file per seeded scenario under `src/CommissionCalculator.Web/Scenarios/`,

   137	  are the seeded scenarios, and their full expected statements are spec.md Appendix A
   138	  (maintainer decision 1A), so SC-001's expected values are the spec's. (Earlier wording, before
   139	  Appendix A: "each seeded rep corresponds to an acceptance example".)

   141	  framework (no package).

   144	
   145	- **Decision**: GitHub Actions on `ubuntu-latest`, `actions/checkout@v7`,
   146	  `actions/setup-dotnet@v6` (reads `global.json`), `actions/upload-artifact@v7`.
   147	- **Established**: source host, 2026-09-21 — latest releases: checkout v7.0.1 (2026-07-20),
   148	  setup-dotnet v6.0.0 (2026-07-16, documents installing the `global.json` SDK when no version is

   155	
   156	- **Decision**: the engine is pure (no I/O, no clock, no statics with state); seed files are
   157	  read-only. CI additionally runs every test in every test project individually
   158	  (`--filter-method` per fully qualified `className.name` read from the suite run's TRX), so a test
   159	  depending on another would fail there.

   161	  argument, but seeds 1, 2 and 3 all ran one class's five tests in the same order (T3, T5, T1, T2,
   162	  T4 — not declaration order), so a different order cannot be forced cheaply. "Any order" is
   163	  therefore enforced by design (no mutable shared state, Principle II) and by the per-test run, not

   182	  `dotnet new webapp` ran with `--network none` (`docker inspect` → `NetworkMode=none`); a

   187	## R17. Seed files reach build and publish output by default

1	# Data Model: Quarterly Sales Commission Calculator
     2	
     3	All money is an exact decimal in USD with at most two decimal places on input (FR-004). Dates are
     4	calendar dates with no time or time zone. Percentages are exact decimals (e.g. `33.335`).
     5	
     6	## Input entities (engine inputs, read from a scenario file)
     7	
     8	### Scenario
     9	| Field | Type | Rules |
    10	|---|---|---|
    11	| `id` | string | Unique across seeded scenarios, else a load error naming it (FR-004); used in the page URL. |
    12	| `name`, `description` | string | Shown in the picker and page heading. |
    13	| `quarter` | Quarter | Must be three whole calendar months starting on the 1st (Edge Cases). |
    14	| `roster` | Rep[] | Reps who receive a statement. At least one; unique `repId` (FR-004). |
    15	| `deals` | Deal[] | The scenario's own deal list, in listed order (FR-008 lists excluded ones). |
    16	| `bookingQuarters` | BookingQuarter[] | Earlier quarters needed to size clawbacks (FR-016). May be empty. |
    17	
    18	### Quarter
    19	| Field | Type | Rules |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `start`, `end` | date | `start` is the 1st of a month; `end` is the last day of the third month. |
    22	
    23	Derived: `Days = end − start + 1`; `Months` = the three calendar months.
    24	
    25	### Rep
    26	| Field | Type | Rules |
    27	|---|---|---|
    28	| `repId`, `name` | string | |
    29	| `quota` | money | > 0, whole cents (FR-004, FR-005). |
    30	| `startDate` | date | On or before `quarter.end` (FR-011). |
    31	| `openingRecoverableBalance` | money | ≥ 0, whole cents, default 0.00 (FR-004, FR-015). |
    32	
    33	### Deal
    34	| Field | Type | Rules |
    35	|---|---|---|
    36	| `dealId` | string | Unique within its quarter's deal list (FR-004). |
    37	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
    38	| `closeDate` | date | Informational only (FR-008). |
    39	| `bookingDate` | date | Decides the quarter (FR-008). |
    40	| `splits` | SplitCredit[] | ≥ 1; percentages sum to exactly 100 (FR-013); each rep at most once (FR-004); every rep's start date ≤ `bookingDate` (FR-011). |
    41	| `refunds` | Refund[] | In listed order; total ≤ `amount` (FR-017). |
    42	
    43	### SplitCredit
    44	| Field | Type | Rules |
    45	|---|---|---|
    46	| `repId` | string | For the scenario's own deals: on the roster (FR-004). For booking-quarter deals: on the roster or in that quarter's `partners`. |
    47	| `percent` | decimal | > 0 and ≤ 100 (FR-004). |
    48	
    49	### Refund
    50	| Field | Type | Rules |
    51	|---|---|---|
    52	| `amount` | money | > 0, whole cents. |
    53	| `date` | date | ≥ the deal's `bookingDate`. |
    54	
    55	### BookingQuarter
    56	| Field | Type | Rules |
    57	|---|---|---|
    58	| `quarter` | Quarter | Three whole calendar months; ends before the scenario quarter starts (FR-004). |
    59	| `reps` | {repId, quota, startDate}[] | For roster reps credited on its deals. `startDate` must equal the roster's (FR-004). |
    60	| `partners` | {repId, startDate}[] | Split partners not on the roster; they get no statement (FR-016). |
    61	| `deals` | Deal[] | All deals booked in it for those reps (each `bookingDate` inside it), with every refund dated before the refund being sized (FR-004). |
    62	
    63	Completeness is checked for every deal that has a refund dated in the scenario quarter and a
    64	booking date before it: its booking quarter must be present and satisfy the rules above,
    65	otherwise the scenario is rejected (FR-004). Such a deal is sized from the booking quarter's copy;
    66	if the scenario's own deal list also lists it (as an excluded deal), the two entries must be
    67	identical, otherwise the data is inconsistent and the scenario is rejected (FR-004).
    68	
    69	## Output entities (engine results)
    70	
    71	### ScenarioResult
    72	Either **Rejected** — a list of `ValidationError {message, requirementId}` (FR-004), no statements
    73	— or **Calculated** — one `RepStatement` per roster rep, in roster order.
    74	
    75	### RepStatement
    76	| Field | Meaning | FR |
    77	|---|---|---|
    78	| `quota`, `proratedQuota` | Full and prorated quota | FR-005, FR-010 |
    79	| `creditedBookings` | Sum of counted credit lines (before refunds) | FR-008, FR-012 |
    80	| `attainment` | `creditedBookings ÷ proratedQuota`, display only (never used for an amount) | FR-009 |
    81	| `commissionBeforeRefunds` | Sum of tier lines | FR-006 |
    82	| `clawbacks` | Sum of clawback lines (may be negative) | FR-016, FR-017 |
    83	| `earnedCommission` | `commissionBeforeRefunds − clawbacks` (may be negative) | FR-015 |
    84	| `drawPaid` | Sum of monthly draw lines | FR-014 |
    85	| `recovered`, `payable`, `closingRecoverableBalance` | Per FR-015 | FR-015 |
    86	| `lines` | Ordered `BreakdownLine`s | FR-003 |
    87	
    88	### BreakdownLine
    89	`{ section, description, amount, requirementId }`. Every amount shown for a rep is a line; each
    90	subtotal equals the sum of the lines above it that it names (FR-018). `requirementId` is always
    91	an FR in spec.md (SC-002).
    92	
    93	## Calculation (per roster rep)
    94	
    95	Definitions used below: `R(x) = round half away from zero to the cent` (FR-018).
    96	
    97	1. **Credit in a quarter Q under an applied-refund set A** — for each deal booked in Q whose
    98	   splits include the rep: `reduced = amount − Σ(refunds of that deal in A)`; allocate `reduced`
    99	   across the deal's splits by largest remainder (FR-012); the rep's share is their credit from
   100	   that deal. Credit = Σ shares.
   101	2. **Prorated quota** (FR-010) — if `startDate > Q.start`:
   102	   `R(quota × (Q.end − startDate + 1) ÷ Q.Days)`, else `quota`. Must not be 0.00 (FR-004).
   103	3. **Commission(Q, A)** (FR-006, FR-007) — `e100 = proratedQuota`, `e150 = R(1.5 × proratedQuota)`;
   104	   lines `R(5% × min(credit, e100))`, `R(8% × clamp(credit − e100, 0, e150 − e100))`,
   105	   `R(12% × max(credit − e150, 0))`, omitting zero slices; commission = Σ lines.
   106	4. **Commission before refunds** = Commission(scenario quarter, ∅). (A refund cannot predate its
   107	   deal's booking date, so no refund applies to a scenario-quarter deal before the quarter.)
   108	5. **Clawbacks** (FR-016, FR-017) — for each booking quarter BQ (the scenario quarter itself, or
   109	   an earlier `bookingQuarter`), order every refund on BQ's deals credited to the rep by
   110	   (date, deal position, refund position). For each refund r dated inside the scenario quarter:
   111	   `clawback(r) = Commission(BQ, earlier(r)) − Commission(BQ, earlier(r) ∪ {r})`, where
   112	   `earlier(r)` is every refund before r in that order. Refunds dated after the scenario quarter
   113	   are ignored for amounts.
   114	6. **Draw** (FR-014) — for each month of the quarter: 0 before the start month; in the start
   115	   month (if the start date is after the 1st) `R(4000 × daysEmployedInMonth ÷ daysInMonth)`;
   116	   otherwise 4,000.00.
   117	7. **Recovery** (FR-015) — `recoverableTotal = opening + drawPaid`; if `earned ≥ 0`:
   118	   `recovered = min(earned, recoverableTotal)`, `payable = earned − recovered`,
   119	   `closing = recoverableTotal − recovered`; else `recovered = payable = 0`,
   120	   `closing = recoverableTotal − earned`.
   121	
   122	## Validation (scenario is rejected, with every error listed, if any fails)
   123	
   124	FR-004 (whole cents, positives, non-negative opening balance, split percent range, rep once per
   125	deal, prorated quota ≠ 0, roster membership, booking-quarter completeness and consistency,
   126	quarter shape, refund date ≥ booking date, refunds ≤ amount), FR-011 (start dates), FR-013
   127	(split sum). Validation runs before any calculation; a rejected scenario has no statements.

     1	# Contract: Commission engine public API
     2

     4	surface the web app and the tests use; everything else is `internal`. Names are the planned C#
     5	names; shapes, not bodies.
     6	
     7	```csharp
     8	namespace CommissionCalculator.Engine;
     9	
    10	public sealed record QuarterPeriod(DateOnly Start, DateOnly End);
    11	
    12	public sealed record RepInput(string RepId, string Name, decimal Quota, DateOnly StartDate,
    13	    decimal OpeningRecoverableBalance = 0m);
    14	
    15	public sealed record SplitCredit(string RepId, decimal Percent);
    16	public sealed record RefundInput(decimal Amount, DateOnly Date);
    17	
    18	public sealed record DealInput(string DealId, decimal Amount, DateOnly CloseDate,
    19	    DateOnly BookingDate, IReadOnlyList<SplitCredit> Splits, IReadOnlyList<RefundInput> Refunds);

     1	# Contract: Seeded scenario file
     2	
     3	One UTF-8 JSON file per scenario in `src/CommissionCalculator.Web/Scenarios/*.json`, read into a

     5	and page heading; every other property maps 1:1 to `ScenarioInput` (engine-api.md), which has no
     6	description because the engine does not use one. Property names are camelCase; dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; money and
     7	percentages are JSON numbers read as `decimal` (exact — research R10). Unknown properties are an
     8	error. A file that is not valid JSON or does not match this shape is reported on the page as a
     9	scenario that failed to load, with the parser's message; it never crashes the app.

=== contracts/ui.md
     1	# Contract: Web UI
     2	
     3	Single Razor Page at `/`, server-rendered, no client script.
     4	
     5	- `GET /` — the scenario picker and the first seeded scenario's results.
     6	- `GET /?scenario={id}` — the picker with `{id}` selected and its results. An unknown id shows a
     7	  "scenario not found" message (HTTP 404) and the picker.

    10	
    11	- `<html lang="en">`, a `<title>` of the form "{scenario name} — Commission Calculator", one
    12	  `<h1>`, a `<main>` landmark, and a skip link to it.
    13	- Picker: `<form method="get">` containing `<label for="scenario">`, `<select id="scenario"
    14	  name="scenario">` with one `<option>` per seeded scenario, and a `<button type="submit">`.
    15	- Rejected scenario: an element with `role="alert"` listing each validation message and its FR.
    16	- Each rep: a `<section aria-labelledby>` headed `<h2>` with the rep's name; a summary `<dl>`

    18	  "80.00%", earned commission, clawbacks, draws paid, draw recovered, commission payable, closing

    21	  **Rule**, and one row per `BreakdownLine`, the Rule cell showing the line's FR ID.
    22	- Amounts are formatted `$#,##0.00` with a leading minus sign for negatives (never colour alone).

## Specification Analysis Report

| ID | Category | Severity | Location(s) | Summary | Recommendation |
|----|----------|----------|-------------|---------|----------------|
| C1 | Inconsistency / Coverage | HIGH | spec.md:437-445; data-model.md:89; contracts/ui.md:17-19; tasks.md:185-186, 201-202 | FR-002 requires a per-rep "clawbacks" value, and the summary `<dl>` shows it. That value is the sum of the clawback lines, e.g. $6,600.00 for Wren. It is not on any breakdown line and cites no FR. This contradicts FR-003 ("every amount is on its own line"), data-model:89 and Principle III. No test checks it: T027's summary fields leave out `Clawbacks` and `Recovered`, and T030 checks the `<dl>` values only for Avery's "80.00%". A UI that showed the wrong engine field in the `<dl>` would still pass. | Ask the maintainer: add a "Clawbacks" subtotal line (FR-016) to FR-003 and Appendix A, or drop the total from FR-002. Then have T030 assert that every `<dl>` value equals the matching engine field. |
| F1 | Coverage gap | HIGH | spec.md:475-477; contracts/ui.md:16-21; spec.md Appendix A (e.g. :630) | FR-008 says the close date "is shown for information only". No contract, Appendix A line or task shows it (grep: close date appears only in tasks.md:269-271 as a crediting check). Appendix A line descriptions omit it, and T060 compares descriptions line for line, so the requirement can't be put into the breakdown either. | Ask the maintainer: remove "is shown" from FR-008, or add the close date to contracts/ui.md and assert it in T030. |
| G1 | Guard cannot fail | HIGH | tasks.md:216-223, 72-73 | T031 says "Run; record failing". Its 2.4.11 check (no `fixed`/`sticky`) and 1.4.12 check (no fixed `height`/`overflow:hidden`) are absence checks, and T004's minimal site.css passes them. No step removes a guard to prove they can fail, which breaks Principle II and standing rule 2. | For each of the two checks, add a guard that inserts a `position: fixed` rule or a fixed `height`, confirms the test fails, and records the result. Add them to T063. |
| T1 | Test-first | MEDIUM | tasks.md:65-71 | T003's failing run (before T004) can't show its assertions failing. T002's web project has `partial class Program` and no entry point. A throwaway build confirmed `CS5001: Program does not contain a static 'Main'`. | In T002, add a minimal `Program.cs` with an empty pipeline, so T003 fails because `/` returns 404. |
| S1 | Untested requirement | MEDIUM | spec.md:579-580; tasks.md:390-395 | SC-003 requires all eight rules to be exercised by a seeded scenario. T060 tests seven and marks rule 8 "satisfied by scope", which changes SC-003 without going back to the maintainer (Principle II). The rule 1 (FR-005) and rule 5 (FR-014/015) checks cannot fail, because every statement has those lines. T060 found and fixed this same problem for rule 7 only. | Ask the maintainer to restate SC-003 for rule 8. Give rules 1 and 5 checks that can fail, for example a draw line below $4,000.00 or a non-zero recovery. |
| S2 | Traceability | LOW | tasks.md:387, 423, 197-199 | T061 says SC-002 is "verified by T030 and T060", but T060 is tagged only `@SC-001 @SC-003`. The trace will attribute SC-002 to T030 alone, and T030 checks FR IDs only for the A.1 input, so FR-010/012/016/017 citations are never checked against spec.md under SC-002. | Tag T060 `@SC-002`. |

R16:175 still says the request comes "from inside the container", which R16:181 disproves. | Record the version and date for both, and correct R16:175. |

The approved `--project` reading appears only in plan.md and research.md, while the constitution's pairwise check still says every pair holds. | Record the reading with a PATCH to C2 and VII. |
